name: Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli Black Hole
description: A rotating black hole in three spacetime dimensions with a negative cosmological constant. It has constant negative curvature everywhere, being anti-de Sitter space with points identified by a discrete boost, and it carries a temperature and an entropy that can be computed exactly.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, with $M = 8Gm/c^2$ and $J = 8Gj/c^3$ for a hole of mass $m$ and angular momentum $j$, and $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions. We write $N^2 = r^2/\ell^2 - M + J^2/(4r^2)$, which vanishes on the horizons $r_\pm^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}M\ell^2\left(1 \pm \sqrt{1 - J^2/(M^2\ell^2)}\right)$.

coordinates.name: Stationary

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$
Mass, dimensionless, $M = 8Gm/c^2$ for a hole of mass $m$, with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Angular momentum, a length, $J = 8Gj/c^3$ for a hole of angular momentum $j$; a horizon exists only for $|J| \le M\ell$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$
Mass, dimensionless, $M = 8Gm/c^2$ for a hole of mass $m$, with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Angular momentum, a length, $J = 8Gj/c^3$ for a hole of angular momentum $j$; a horizon exists only for $|J| \le M\ell$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \tilde\phi)$, with the advanced time $v$ a length, $dv = c\,dt + dr/N^2$ and $d\tilde\phi = d\phi + J\,dr/(2r^2N^2)$.

coordinates.name: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$
Mass, dimensionless, $M = 8Gm/c^2$ for a hole of mass $m$, with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Angular momentum, a length, $J = 8Gj/c^3$ for a hole of angular momentum $j$; a horizon exists only for $|J| \le M\ell$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(u, r, \tilde\phi)$, with the retarded time $u$ a length, $du = c\,dt - dr/N^2$ and $d\tilde\phi = d\phi - J\,dr/(2r^2N^2)$.
